thread:
maya: Quick sync 12: ran the ownership-demarcation experiment on cohort-B last night. Functional correctness holds, but we saw p95 latency and GPU-util tails spike. tagging @sanjay and @owen for perf/infra visibility.
sanjay: can you post the perf snapshot and what looks off?
maya: numbers from 02:00-05:00 UTC window:
```
cohort: B
requests: 420k
p50 latency: 34ms
p95 latency: 420ms
p99 latency: 1.2s
avg gpu util: 68%
peak gpu util: 98% (brief spikes)
cache hit rate: 12% (vs 31% baseline)
```
maya: hypothesis: the new ownership routing introduces an adapter hop that reduces cache locality for many long-context requests; batching got desynced for some sequence-length distributions which caused larger KV repop windows.
owen: any errors or 5xx spikes?
maya: no 5xx spike, error budget fine, but some per-route latency SLOs were near threshold for a few major customers.
lucy: did the rollout touch batching config or quantization?
maya: only routing + lightweight adapter. batching and quant profiles unchanged. routing increased cross-pod fanout for long contexts.
sanjay: two asks: (1) add per-pod cache-hit heatmap keyed by ownership tag, (2) run a synthetic replay to measure desync effects.
maya: (1) done on test cluster, ownership_tag->pod->cache_hit heatmap added. (2) scheduling a replay job tomorrow against sampled traffic.
owen: any quick mitigations we can flip now? e.g., rollback routing for cohort-B, enable affinity, or prewarm caches?
maya: options sketched:
- rollback cohort-B to prior routing (fast)
- enable soft affinity: prefer last-known pod for session tokens
- adjust batching window to reduce desync for long contexts
- prewarm hot prefixes on rollout
I think soft affinity + prewarm is lowest risk.
lucy: agree. I'll draft runbook updates for ownership semantics and rollback steps.
infra-bot: deploy job #r-2024-443 applied to cluster-staging by maya (2024-06-11T02:13:45Z)
sanjay: gate full rollout on heatmap threshold: abort if per-pod cache-hit delta > 10% for any major tenant. Also automated abort if tenant p95 > 1.2x baseline during canary window.
maya: will implement heatmap threshold and 1h canary window; automate abort on p95 >20% over baseline per tenant.
owen: dedicated pools might see noisy-neighbor effects; do we need reserved buffer?
maya: capacity confirmed small reserved buffer and affinity priority for dedicated pools; added to checklist.
lucy: post-replay we'll do a short follow-up: owners, actions, ETAs. I'll own docs + checklist.
sanjay: timeline?
maya: replay tomorrow morning; heatmap available ~2h after replay completes. If any tenant >8% cache loss, rollback. I'll post results EOD.
lucy: action items: (1) docs + rollback runbook (lucy) (2) affinity shim + flag (owen + maya) (3) prewarm list for top-50 prefixes per tenant (maya).
owen: building small shim, feature-flagged; aim to land by 09:00 UTC.
infra-bot: monitor alert created: ownership-demarcation.p95 > baseline*1.2 (alert id ad-3142)
maya: overall: experiment validates ownership semantics and reduces cross-tenant entanglement in happy path. We'll continue but require mitigations before broad rollout.
sanjay: thanks maya, good experiment. reconvene after replay. :thumbsup:
